question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 1 Practice Paper (SSS & SAS Focus)

questions.question_text: If two triangles ΔABC and ΔXYZ satisfy AB = XY, BC = YZ, and AC = XZ, which congruence condition guarantees their congruence?
In ΔPQR and ΔDEF, PQ = DE, QR = EF, and ∠Q = ∠E. Which criterion proves ΔPQR ≅ ΔDEF?
If ΔHEN ≅ ΔBIG, list all 3 pairs of equal corresponding sides and all 3 pairs of equal corresponding angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Corresponding sides: HE = BI, EN = IG, HN = BG. Corresponding angles: ∠H = ∠B, ∠E = ∠I, ∠N = ∠G.

questions.question_text: Why does Side-Side-Angle (SSA) fail to guarantee triangle congruence in general non-right triangles?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In general non-right triangles, a non-included angle allows two different triangular shapes (one acute, one obtuse) to be constructed with the same two side lengths.

questions.question_text: In quadrilateral ABCD, side AB = AD and side CB = CD. Prove that diagonal AC bisects ∠BAD and ∠BCD.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In ΔABC and ΔADC: 1) AB = AD (Given), 2) CB = CD (Given), 3) AC = AC (Common side). By SSS, ΔABC ≅ ΔADC. By CPCT, ∠BAC = ∠DAC (so AC bisects ∠BAD) and ∠BCA = ∠DCA (so AC bisects ∠BCD).

questions.question_text: An architectural bridge truss features two symmetric triangular frames ΔPQS and ΔRQS joined at vertical beam QS. Given PQ = RQ = 12 m and ∠PQS = ∠RQS = 40°. (a) Prove ΔPQS ≅ ΔRQS. (b) If PS = 8 m, find length RS.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) In ΔPQS and ΔRQS: PQ = RQ = 12m, ∠PQS = ∠RQS = 40°, QS = QS. By SAS, ΔPQS ≅ ΔRQS. (b) By CPCT, RS = PS = 8 m.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 1 Practice Paper (ASA, AAS & RHS Focus)

questions.question_text: In right-angled ΔABC (∠B=90°) and ΔDEF (∠E=90°), hypotenuse AC = DF and side BC = EF. Which criterion establishes ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF?
Which condition guarantees similarity but NOT congruence between two triangles?
In ΔABC and ΔPQR, ∠A = ∠P = 50°, ∠B = ∠Q = 60°, and included side AB = PQ = 7 cm. Are the triangles congruent? State the criterion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yes, ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR by ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) criterion because two angles and the included side are equal.

questions.question_text: State the full form and definition of the RHS congruence criterion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: RHS stands for Right-Hypotenuse-Side. If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the other, the triangles are congruent.

questions.question_text: In right-angled ΔABC (∠B = 90°) and right-angled ΔPQR (∠Q = 90°), hypotenuse AC = 10 cm, leg BC = 6 cm, hypotenuse PR = 10 cm, and leg QR = 6 cm. Prove ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR and find side AB if PQ = 8 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) In right ΔABC and ΔPQR, ∠B = ∠Q = 90°, AC = PR = 10 cm (Hypotenuse), BC = QR = 6 cm (Leg). By RHS criterion, ΔABC ≅ ΔPQR. 2) By CPCT, AB = PQ = 8 cm.

questions.question_text: A surveyor measures two right-triangular land plots ΔLMN (∠M=90°) and ΔXYZ (∠Y=90°). He finds LN = XZ = 25 m and MN = YZ = 15 m. (a) State why ΔLMN ≅ ΔXYZ. (b) If LM = 20 m, calculate XY. (c) Find area of plot LMN.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) ΔLMN ≅ ΔXYZ by RHS criterion. (b) By CPCT, XY = LM = 20 m. (c) Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 15 × 20 = 150 sq meters.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 1 Practice Paper (Isosceles & Equilateral Properties)

questions.question_text: In ΔABC, if side AB = AC and ∠A = 40°, what is the measure of ∠B?
What is the measure of each interior angle in an equilateral triangle?
State the Isosceles Triangle Theorem regarding angles opposite to equal sides.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In any triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure. If AB = AC in ΔABC, then ∠B = ∠C.

questions.question_text: In ΔPQR, PQ = PR and ∠Q = 65°. Find the measures of ∠R and ∠P.
In ΔABC, line segment AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC. Prove that ΔABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In ΔABD and ΔACD: 1) BD = CD (AD bisects BC), 2) ∠ADB = ∠ADC = 90° (AD ⊥ BC), 3) AD = AD (Common). By SAS criterion, ΔABD ≅ ΔACD. By CPCT, AB = AC. Thus ΔABC is isosceles.

questions.question_text: A craft worker makes an isosceles triangular pennant ΔXYZ where XY = XZ. The vertex angle ∠X measures 50°. (a) Find base angles ∠Y and ∠Z. (b) If she cuts an identical pennant ΔX'Y'Z', verify if ΔXYZ ≅ ΔX'Y'Z' when YZ = Y'Z' = 6 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) ∠Y = ∠Z = (180° - 50°)/2 = 65°. (b) In ΔXYZ and ΔX'Y'Z', ∠Y = ∠Y' = 65°, YZ = Y'Z' = 6 cm, ∠Z = ∠Z' = 65°. By ASA criterion, the two pennants are congruent.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 1 Practice Paper (Notation & Proof Applications)

questions.question_text: If ΔABC ≅ ΔFDG, which of the following is a true statement of equality?
If ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ, which angle corresponds to ∠R?
If ΔCAT ≅ ΔDOG, list all valid permutations of expressing this congruence statement.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: ΔCAT ≅ ΔDOG, ΔCTA ≅ ΔDGO, ΔACT ≅ ΔODG, ΔATC ≅ ΔOGD, ΔTCA ≅ ΔGOD, ΔTAC ≅ ΔGDO.

questions.question_text: What does CPCT stand for in triangle geometry?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: CPCT stands for 'Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles' (which are always equal).

questions.question_text: Lines AB and CD bisect each other at O. Prove that: (i) ΔAOC ≅ ΔBOD, (ii) AC || BD.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) In ΔAOC and ΔBOD: AO = BO (O bisects AB), CO = DO (O bisects CD), ∠AOC = ∠BOD (Vertically opposite angles). By SAS, ΔAOC ≅ ΔBOD. (ii) By CPCT, ∠OAC = ∠OBD. Since alternate interior angles are equal, AC || BD.

questions.question_text: A teacher draws two triangles on the board: ΔABC with AB=5cm, BC=6cm, AC=7cm and ΔDEF with DE=5cm, EF=6cm, DF=7cm. (a) Express the congruence using correct vertex order. (b) Find ∠E if ∠B = 78°.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF (since AB=DE, BC=EF, AC=DF). (b) By CPCT, ∠E = ∠B = 78°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 1 Practice Paper (Rigid Transformations & Superimposition)

questions.question_text: Which transformation slides a figure without flipping or turning it?
Why are translation, rotation, and reflection called rigid motions?
options: B) They preserve distances and angles
questions.correct_answer: B) They preserve distances and angles

questions.question_text: Explain how superimposition is used to test whether two plane figures are congruent.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Trace one figure on tracing paper and place it over the second figure. If it covers the second figure exactly without gaps or overlaps, the figures are congruent.

questions.question_text: Are any two squares with side length 5 cm congruent? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yes, because all squares have equal 90° angles (same shape) and equal side lengths 5 cm (same size), so one superimposes perfectly onto the other.

questions.question_text: In figure ABCD with AB || CD and AD || BC (a parallelogram), prove that diagonal AC divides it into two congruent triangles ΔABC ≅ ΔCDA.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In ΔABC and ΔCDA: 1) ∠BAC = ∠DCA (Alternate interior angles as AB || CD), 2) AC = CA (Common side), 3) ∠BCA = ∠DAC (Alternate interior angles as AD || BC). By ASA criterion, ΔABC ≅ ΔCDA.

questions.question_text: A graphic designer creates a logo using two overlapping congruent triangles ΔPQR and ΔSTU. Given PQ = ST = 8 cm, QR = TU = 10 cm, and PR = SU = 12 cm. (a) Identify the congruence condition. (b) If ∠P = 55°, find ∠S. (c) What rigid motion maps ΔPQR onto ΔSTU?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) SSS Criterion. (b) By CPCT, ∠S = ∠P = 55°. (c) A combination of translation and rotation (rigid motion).

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 2 Practice Paper (Token Model & Additive Inverses)

questions.question_text: In the token model, what is the net value of one green token (+1) and one red token (-1)?
What is the additive inverse of -25?
Define a 'Zero Pair' in the token model and write its mathematical equation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A Zero Pair consists of one positive (+1) token and one negative (-1) token combined together, having a net value of 0: (+1) + (-1) = 0.

questions.question_text: Explain how subtracting an integer is equivalent to adding its additive inverse. Illustrate with (-7) - (+4) and (-7) - (-4).
A bank account shows a balance of ₹500. Over 4 days, transactions are: Deposit ₹200, Withdraw ₹350, Withdraw ₹150, Deposit ₹100. (a) Express each transaction as an integer. (b) Find final balance.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 2 Practice Paper (Integer Multiplication Sign Rules)

questions.question_text: What is the product of (-14) × (-5)?
What is the sign of the product when five negative integers are multiplied together?
State the general sign rules for multiplying two integers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Like signs produce a positive product: (+)×(+) = +, (-)×(-) = +. 2) Unlike signs produce a negative product: (+)×(-) = -, (-)×(+) = -.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how the token model explains (-3) × (-4) = +12 starting with an empty bag.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Multiplier -3 means removing 4 negative (red) tokens 3 times. 2) Insert 12 zero pairs (12 green + 12 red) into empty bag. 3) Remove 12 red tokens. 4) Remaining tokens in bag are 12 green (+1) tokens, proving (-3) × (-4) = +12.

questions.question_text: A cold storage facility drops temperature at 3°C per hour from an initial temperature of 15°C. (a) Write the temperature change rate as an integer. (b) Calculate temperature after 8 hours.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Rate = -3°C per hour. (b) Change in 8 hours = 8 × (-3) = -24°C. Final temp = 15 + (-24) = -9°C.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 2 Practice Paper (Integer Division)

questions.question_text: What is 36 ÷ (-18)?
Explain why division of integers is the inverse operation of multiplication.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: If a × b = c, then c ÷ b = a and c ÷ a = b. For example, since (-4) × (-5) = 20, then 20 ÷ (-5) = -4.

questions.question_text: In a test, (+4) marks are given for every correct answer and (-2) marks for every incorrect answer. (a) Radhika scored 20 marks with 8 correct answers. How many incorrect answers did she give? (b) Jay scored -6 marks with 3 correct answers. How many incorrect answers did he give?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Correct score = 8 × 4 = 32. Incorrect score = 20 - 32 = -12. Incorrect count = (-12) ÷ (-2) = 6. (b) Correct score = 3 × 4 = 12. Incorrect score = -6 - 12 = -18. Incorrect count = (-18) ÷ (-2) = 9.

questions.question_text: A elevator in a mine shaft descends at a speed of 6 meters per minute starting from 10 meters above ground level (+10 m). (a) Write its position formula. (b) Find its position after 20 minutes. (c) How long will it take to reach -110 m?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Position = 10 - 6t. (b) After 20 min = 10 - 6(20) = 10 - 120 = -110 m. (c) Time = (Distance to descend 120 m) / 6 = 20 minutes.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 2 Practice Paper (Distributive Property)

questions.question_text: Which expression illustrates the Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition?
Evaluate 18 × (-99) using the distributive property.
Use distributive property to evaluate: (-25) × 102.
Verify distributive property for a = -3, b = 4, c = -2.

A cement company earns profit ₹8 per white bag sold and loss ₹5 per grey bag sold. (a) If it sells 3000 white bags and 5000 grey bags, find net profit/loss. (b) How many white bags must it sell to have zero profit/loss if 6400 grey bags are sold?

A submarine at sea level (0 m) descends at 5 m/min. Simultaneously, a drone at +30 m descends at 2 m/min. (a) Write submarine position after 10 min. (b) Write drone position after 10 min. (c) Find vertical distance between them at t = 10 min.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Submarine = 10 × (-5) = -50 m. (b) Drone = 30 - (10 × 2) = +10 m. (c) Distance = 10 - (-50) = 60 meters.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 2 Practice Paper (Comprehensive Integer Word Problems)

questions.question_text: Find three consecutive integers whose product is -24.
Which expression equals zero?
Find a pair of integers whose sum is -7 and product is 12.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The integers are -3 and -4 because (-3) + (-4) = -7 and (-3) × (-4) = +12.

questions.question_text: Evaluate: [(-36) ÷ 12] ÷ 3 vs (-36) ÷ [12 ÷ 3]. Is division associative?

A shopkeeper earns ₹1 profit on selling a pen and incurs a loss of 40 paise (₹0.40) per pencil. (a) In one month he incurs a loss of ₹5 after selling 45 pens. How many pencils did he sell? (b) Next month he earns no profit/loss; if he sells 70 pens, how many pencils were sold?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Profit on pens = 45 × 1 = ₹45. Total loss = -₹5. Loss on pencils = -5 - 45 = -₹50 = -5000 paise. Pencils sold = 5000 / 40 = 125 pencils. (b) Profit on pens = ₹70. Loss on pencils needed = ₹70 = 7000 paise. Pencils sold = 7000 / 40 = 175 pencils.

questions.question_text: A mountain climber starts at +1200 m above sea level. He climbs up 350 m, then descends 600 m due to bad weather, and finally climbs up 250 m. (a) Represent each movement as an integer. (b) Calculate his final altitude.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) +350, -600, +250. (b) Final altitude = 1200 + 350 - 600 + 250 = 1200 m above sea level.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (HCF & Floor Tiling Focus)

questions.question_text: What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
To cover a room floor with the largest possible identical square tiles without cutting, the side length of the tile must equal:
Define Highest Common Factor (HCF) or Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The HCF (or GCD) of two or more numbers is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers completely without leaving a remainder.

questions.question_text: Find the HCF of 24, 36, and 60 by prime factorisation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 24 = 2³×3, 36 = 2²×3², 60 = 2²×3×5. Common prime factors with lowest powers = 2² × 3¹ = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.question_text: A hall floor measures 18 m by 24 m. Sameeksha wants to tile it with square tiles of maximum size without cutting any tile. (a) Find maximum tile side. (b) Find total number of tiles needed.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Tile side = HCF(18, 24) = 6 meters. (b) Tiles along length = 24/6 = 4. Tiles along width = 18/6 = 3. Total tiles = 4 × 3 = 12 tiles.

questions.question_text: A charity distributes 225 kg of rice and 750 kg of wheat in bags of equal weight containing either only rice or only wheat. (a) Find maximum weight of each bag. (b) How many bags of rice and wheat are created?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Maximum weight = HCF(225, 750). 225 = 3²×5², 750 = 2×3×5³. HCF = 3¹×5² = 75 kg. (b) Rice bags = 225/75 = 3 bags. Wheat bags = 750/75 = 10 bags. Total = 13 bags.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (LCM & Periodic Cycles Focus)

questions.question_text: What is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
If two numbers are co-prime, what is their LCM?
Anshu uses 6 cm cloth strips and Guna uses 8 cm strips to make torans of equal length. Find the shortest possible length of their toran.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Shortest length = LCM(6, 8) = 24 cm.

questions.question_text: Find the LCM of 15, 20, and 30 using prime factorisation.
Three traffic signals change color every 12 seconds, 18 seconds, and 24 seconds respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 9:00 AM, at what time will they change together next?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Find LCM(12, 18, 24). 12 = 2²×3, 18 = 2×3², 24 = 2³×3. LCM = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72 seconds = 1 min 12 sec. Next simultaneous change = 9:01:12 AM.

questions.question_text: Three bells toll together at intervals of 9, 12, and 15 minutes. (a) Calculate LCM(9, 12, 15). (b) Convert time to hours. (c) If they toll at 6:00 AM, when will they toll together next?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 9 = 3², 12 = 2²×3, 15 = 3×5. LCM = 2²×3²×5 = 180 minutes. (b) 180 / 60 = 3 hours. (c) Next toll time = 6:00 AM + 3 hours = 9:00 AM.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (Prime Factorisation Method)

questions.question_text: What is the prime factorisation of 360?
When computing HCF from prime factorisations, which exponent is chosen for each common prime factor?
Write the prime factorisations of 45 and 36, and find their HCF.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 45 = 3² × 5; 36 = 2² × 3². Common prime factor is 3 with lowest power 3². HCF = 9.

questions.question_text: Write the prime factorisations of 45 and 36, and find their LCM.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 45 = 3² × 5; 36 = 2² × 3². All prime factors with max powers: 2², 3², 5¹. LCM = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180.

questions.question_text: Express 144, 180, and 192 as products of prime factors. Calculate both HCF(144, 180, 192) and LCM(144, 180, 192).

A school sports coordinator wants to arrange 108 boys and 144 girls into equal rows containing either only boys or only girls. (a) Find maximum number of students per row. (b) Find total number of rows formed.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Max per row = HCF(108, 144). 108 = 2²×3³, 144 = 2⁴×3². HCF = 2²×3² = 36 students per row. (b) Boys rows = 108/36 = 3. Girls rows = 144/36 = 4. Total rows = 7.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (HCF-LCM Formula & Co-Primes)

questions.question_text: The HCF of two numbers is 9 and their LCM is 180. If one number is 45, what is the other number?
Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
State the formula relating HCF, LCM, and two numbers 'a' and 'b'. Does this formula hold for three numbers?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. No, this formula does NOT hold for three numbers.

questions.question_text: The HCF of two co-prime numbers is 1 and their LCM is 66. Find two possible pairs of numbers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Since HCF = 1, a × b = 66. Co-prime factor pairs of 66: (1, 66), (2, 33), (3, 22), (6, 11). Any two pairs are valid.

questions.question_text: The product of two numbers is 2160 and their HCF is 12. (a) Find their LCM. (b) If one number is 60, find the other number. (c) Verify that HCF × LCM = Product.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) LCM = 2160 / 12 = 180. (b) Other number = 2160 / 60 = 36. (c) HCF × LCM = 12 × 180 = 2160 = Product verified.

questions.question_text: Two ropes of lengths 64 cm and 80 cm are to be cut into pieces of equal length. (a) Find maximum length of each piece. (b) Find total pieces obtained. (c) Verify HCF(64,80) × LCM(64,80) = 64 × 80.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 3 Practice Paper (Advanced Word Problems)

questions.question_text: What is the smallest 3-digit number divisible by 6, 8, and 12?
What is the largest number that divides 70 and 125 leaving remainders 5 and 8 respectively?
Find the greatest number that divides 615 and 963 leaving a remainder of 6 in each case.
Can two numbers have 15 as their HCF and 110 as their LCM? Give reasons.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No, because the HCF must always divide the LCM completely. 110 is not divisible by 15 (110 ÷ 15 = 7.33).

questions.question_text: Find the smallest number which when divided by 12, 16, 24, and 36 leaves a remainder of 7 in each case.

A sweet seller has 420 kaju barfis and 130 badam barfis. She wants to stack them in equal counts such that they take up minimum tray space. (a) Find maximum number of barfis per stack. (b) Find number of stacks for each type.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Stack count = HCF(420, 130) = 10 barfis per stack. (b) Kaju stacks = 420/10 = 42; Badam stacks = 130/10 = 13 stacks.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 4 Practice Paper (Place Value & Fraction Conversion)

questions.question_text: What is the place value of digit 3 in 27.53?
Convert 2/5 into decimal form.
Write 27.53 in expanded form showing place values.
Convert into decimal form using equivalent fractions: (a) 13/4, (b) 4/50, (c) 5/8.
Four friends want to divide a 29-meter roll of ribbon equally among themselves. (a) Express share as fraction. (b) Convert fraction to decimal. (c) How many meters does each friend receive?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Share = 29 / 4. (b) 29 / 4 = (29 × 25) / (4 × 25) = 725 / 100 = 7.25. (c) Each friend receives 7.25 meters of ribbon.

questions.question_text: A grocery store lists items per kg: Sugar ₹42.50, Rice ₹58.25, Flour ₹32.80. (a) Convert 1/4 kg sugar to decimal weight. (b) Cost of 1/4 kg sugar. (c) Total cost of 2 kg rice and 500 g flour.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 4 Practice Paper (Decimal Multiplication)

questions.question_text: State the rule for placing decimal point when multiplying two decimal numbers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiply the numbers as whole integers, then count total decimal places in both factors and place decimal point that many places from the right in the product.

questions.question_text: A rectangular garden plot is 12.4 meters long and 8.5 meters wide. (a) Calculate area of garden. (b) If fencing costs ₹45.50 per meter, calculate total cost to fence perimeter.
A car covers 16.5 km per liter of petrol. Fuel tank holds 35.5 liters. (a) How far can car travel on a full tank? (b) If petrol costs ₹96.50 per liter, calculate cost of full tank.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 4 Practice Paper (Decimal Division Methods)

questions.question_text: Explain the decimal shift method for dividing 22.5 by 0.5.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiply both dividend and divisor by 10 to clear divisor decimal: (22.5 × 10) / (0.5 × 10) = 225 / 5 = 45.

questions.question_text: A vehicle covers a distance of 43.2 km in 2.4 liters of petrol. (a) Calculate distance covered per liter. (b) How many liters are needed for 108 km?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Distance per liter = 43.2 ÷ 2.4 = 432 ÷ 24 = 18 km per liter. (b) Petrol required = 108 / 18 = 6 liters.

questions.question_text: A tailor has a roll of cloth measuring 37.8 meters. Each shirt requires 1.8 meters of cloth. (a) How many shirts can be stitched? (b) If each shirt sells for ₹450.50, find total earnings.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 4 Practice Paper (Metric Unit Conversions)

questions.question_text: Convert 35 cm into meters.
Convert 68 grams into kilograms.
Convert: (a) 5.5 km to meters, (b) 125.5 mL to liters.
Express in kg using decimals: 5 kg 8 g and 25 kg 750 g.
Each side of a regular polygon is 2.5 cm long. Its perimeter is 12.5 cm. (a) Calculate number of sides. (b) Identify name of polygon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Number of sides = Perimeter / Side length = 12.5 / 2.5 = 125 / 25 = 5 sides. (b) Name = Regular Pentagon.

questions.question_text: A juice vendor buys 15.5 L of orange juice. He serves it in small cups of capacity 250 mL (0.25 L). (a) Convert 15.5 L to mL. (b) How many cups can he serve? (c) If each cup costs ₹15, find total income.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 4 Practice Paper (Patiganita & Combined Word Problems)

questions.question_text: Which ancient Indian mathematical text contains division problems convertible into modern decimal operations?
What is 0.2 × 0.3?
A sheet of paper is 0.12 mm thick. Find total thickness of a stack of 500 such sheets in cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total thickness in mm = 500 × 0.12 = 60 mm. Convert to cm = 60 / 10 = 6 cm.

questions.question_text: A chef requires 0.45 kg of flour to bake one cake. He has 11.25 kg of flour. (a) How many cakes can he bake? (b) If he bakes 18 cakes, how much flour is left?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Cakes = 11.25 / 0.45 = 1125 / 45 = 25 cakes. (b) Flour used for 18 cakes = 18 × 0.45 = 8.1 kg. Flour left = 11.25 - 8.1 = 3.15 kg.

questions.question_text: A school buys 45 notebooks at ₹28.50 each and 30 pens at ₹15.25 each. (a) Total cost of notebooks. (b) Total cost of pens. (c) Overall bill amount.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 5 Practice Paper (Arithmetic Mean & Fair-Share Concept)

questions.question_text: What is the formula for Arithmetic Mean?
options: A) Sum of values × Total number
B) Sum of values / Total number
questions.correct_answer: B) Sum of values / Total number

questions.question_text: What is the mean of the first five prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11)?
Explain why the Arithmetic Mean is conceptualized as a 'fair-share' value.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mean represents redistributing the total combined quantity equally among all individuals in a group so that everyone receives an equal share.

questions.question_text: Find the mean of marks scored by 5 students: 14, 18, 12, 20, 16.
The mean mark of 6 students in a test is 18. If one student who scored 8 marks is excluded, calculate the new mean of the remaining 5 students.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Original total marks = 18 × 6 = 108. New total after excluding 8 = 108 - 8 = 100. New mean = 100 / 5 = 20.

questions.question_text: Daily rainfall in mm for a week: 5.6, 8.0, 3.0, 12.0, 6.5, 12.1, 11.2. (a) Find maximum and minimum rainfall. (b) Find range. (c) Calculate mean daily rainfall.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 5 Practice Paper (Median Calculation & Ordered Datasets)

questions.question_text: What is the median of the dataset: 7, 2, 9, 4, 5?
How is median calculated when dataset has an even number N of observations?
options: B) Average of N/2 and (N/2)+1 positions
questions.correct_answer: B) Average of N/2 and (N/2)+1 positions

questions.question_text: Find the median of heights (in cm): 142, 138, 145, 140, 144, 139.
Is the median always one of the numbers given in the raw dataset? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. When N is even, median is the average of two central values, which may yield a decimal/value not present in raw data.

questions.question_text: Heights of 17 students (cm): 106, 110, 123, 125, 117, 120, 112, 115, 110, 120, 115, 102, 115, 115, 109, 115, 101. (a) Sort data. (b) Find median height. (c) Divide into 2 equal groups above/below median.
Scores of 9 students in a quiz: 12, 15, 11, 18, 20, 15, 14, 15, 16. (a) Find mean score. (b) Find median score. (c) Find mode score.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Sum = 136, Mean = 136/9 = 15.11. (b) Sorted: 11, 12, 14, 15, 15, 15, 16, 18, 20. Median = 5th value = 15. (c) Mode = 15 (appears 3 times).

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 5 Practice Paper (Dot Plots & Outlier Sensitivity)

questions.question_text: What is an outlier in a statistical dataset?
options: B) An extreme value far removed from the main cluster
questions.correct_answer: B) An extreme value far removed from the main cluster

questions.question_text: Which measure of central tendency is heavily distorted/pulled by extreme outliers?
Describe the structure and purpose of a Dot Plot.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A Dot Plot displays discrete data values as stacked dots above a number line, revealing data distribution, clusters, gaps, range, and outliers.

questions.question_text: Dataset: {10, 12, 11, 13, 12, 11, 85}. Identify outlier and explain its effect on mean vs median.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Outlier = 85. Mean with outlier = 150/7 = 21.4 (heavily inflated). Median = 12. Removing 85: Mean = 69/6 = 11.5; Median = 11.5. Median is stable while mean is heavily distorted.

questions.question_text: Poovizhi collected storybooks read by 7 students: 3, 4, 3, 5, 4, 3, 28. (a) Calculate mean with outlier 28. (b) Calculate median. (c) Remove outlier 28 and recalculate mean and median. (d) State conclusion.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Mean = 50 / 7 = 7.14 books. (b) Sorted: 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 28. Median = 4 books. (c) Without 28: Mean = 22 / 6 = 3.67 books; Median = 3.5 books. (d) Outlier inflates mean by ~3.5 books while median changes by only 0.5 books.

questions.question_text: Number of letters in names of 10 students: 4, 5, 6, 4, 5, 7, 4, 5, 6, 14. (a) Identify clusters and outlier. (b) Find median name length. (c) Find mean name length.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Cluster = 4-7 letters; Outlier = 14 letters. (b) Sorted: 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 14. Median = (5+5)/2 = 5 letters. (c) Mean = 60 / 10 = 6 letters.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 5 Practice Paper (Clustered Bar Graphs & Axis Cropping)

questions.question_text: Why is a cropped vertical axis (starting above 0) used on bar graphs?
options: B) To zoom in and highlight small differences in large values
questions.correct_answer: B) To zoom in and highlight small differences in large values

questions.question_text: What type of graph places twin vertical bars side-by-side for each category to compare two groups?
Explain when a double bar graph is preferred over a single bar graph.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A double bar graph is preferred when comparing two sets of related data simultaneously across the same categories (e.g., marks of boys vs girls, or prices in two different towns).

questions.question_text: Onion prices (₹/kg) in Yahapur vs Wahapur over 3 months: Jan (30 vs 35), Feb (40 vs 42), Mar (50 vs 45). Calculate mean price in each town.

Pocket counts survey: Boys: {2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7}; Girls: {0, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4}. (a) Calculate median pocket count for boys and girls. (b) Calculate mean pocket count for boys and girls. (c) Compare data distributions.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Boys median = 5, Girls median = 2. (b) Boys mean = 41 / 9 = 4.56; Girls mean = 14 / 7 = 2.0. (c) Boys' garments have significantly higher pocket counts (center around 4-5) compared to girls' garments (center around 2).

questions.question_text: A school sports day recorded jump distances (m) for two houses: Ruby: {1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 1.8, 2.1}; Emerald: {1.3, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9}. (a) Find median jump distance for Ruby and Emerald. (b) Which house had higher overall performance?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Ruby median = 1.5 m; Emerald median = 1.6 m. (b) Emerald mean = 8.0 / 5 = 1.6 m; Ruby mean = 8.0 / 5 = 1.6 m. Both have equal mean performance, but Emerald has a higher median.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 5 Practice Paper (Comprehensive Data Interpretation)

questions.question_text: Which measure of central tendency can never be greater than the maximum data value?
What is the mode of dataset: 5, 8, 5, 3, 5, 8, 9?
Can mean or median lie outside the minimum and maximum boundaries of a dataset? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Both mean and median must lie strictly within the closed interval [min, max] of the dataset.

questions.question_text: Find mean, median, and mode for data: 12, 15, 12, 18, 20, 12, 17.
The average weight of 10 students is 42 kg. When the weight of a teacher is added, average weight increases to 44 kg. Calculate teacher's weight.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Original total weight = 10 × 42 = 420 kg. New total weight with teacher (11 persons) = 11 × 44 = 484 kg. Teacher's weight = 484 - 420 = 64 kg.

questions.question_text: Data of hours spent studying by 8 students: 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 2, 9. (a) Calculate mean. (b) Calculate median. (c) Identify outlier. (d) Which measure better represents typical study hours?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Mean = 28 / 8 = 3.5 hours. (b) Sorted: 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9. Median = (2+3)/2 = 2.5 hours. (c) Outlier = 9 hours. (d) Median (2.5 hrs) better represents typical study time because mean is inflated by the outlier 9.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Perpendicular Bisector & Equidistance)

questions.question_text: What compass radius setting is required when constructing the perpendicular bisector of segment XY?
options: B) Strictly greater than half of XY (>0.5 XY)
C) Less than half of XY
questions.correct_answer: B) Strictly greater than half of XY (>0.5 XY)

questions.question_text: Any point located on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB is:
options: A) Equidistant from endpoints A and B
B) Closer to A than B
C) At right angles to midpoint only
questions.correct_answer: A) Equidistant from endpoints A and B

questions.question_text: Which two classical instruments are exclusively permitted in geometric constructions?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An unmarked straightedge (ruler) and a pair of compasses.

questions.question_text: Is it necessary to use the same compass radius for arcs above and below segment XY when constructing its perpendicular bisector? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Radius for top arcs can differ from bottom arcs, provided top arcs from X and Y are equal to each other (>0.5 XY) and bottom arcs from X and Y are equal to each other.

questions.question_text: Draw segment XY = 8 cm. Describe step-by-step how to construct its perpendicular bisector line AB using ruler and compass. Prove why AX = AY.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Steps: 1) Draw XY = 8 cm. 2) Set compass radius > 4 cm. Draw arcs above and below XY from X and Y meeting at A and B. 3) Join AB meeting XY at M. Proof: In ΔAMX and ΔAMY, MX = MY, ∠AMX = ∠AMY = 90°, AM = AM. By SAS, ΔAMX ≅ ΔAMY, so AX = AY by CPCT.

questions.question_text: An artist constructs a symmetrical human eye outline. The upper and lower eyelid arcs meet at corners P and Q (PQ = 6 cm). (a) What line contains the center points for both arcs? (b) Prove that any center point C on this line satisfies CP = CQ.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) The center points lie on the perpendicular bisector of segment PQ. (b) By SAS triangle congruence (ΔCMP ≅ ΔCMQ where M is midpoint of PQ), CP = CQ.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Angle Bisector & Copying Angles)

questions.question_text: Which triangle congruence criterion is applied when copying an angle using ruler and compass?
An angle bisector divides an angle of 74° into two angles measuring:
Describe step-by-step how to bisect a given angle ∠AOB.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Draw an arc from vertex O intersecting arms OA and OB at P and Q. 2) From P and Q, draw equal arcs intersecting at C. 3) Ray OC is the angle bisector.

questions.question_text: If ray OC bisects ∠AOB and ∠AOC = 28°, find the measure of ∠AOB.
Describe step-by-step how to construct a line parallel to line 'l' passing through an external point P using alternate interior angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Pick point A on line 'l' and draw transversal AP. 2) ∠PAL is formed. 3) At vertex P, copy ∠PAL on alternate side of transversal AP using SSS angle copy method to form ∠APM = ∠PAL. 4) Extend ray PM to form line 'm' parallel to 'l'.

questions.question_text: A carpenter wants to cut two wood panels at identical angles ∠ABC = 52°. He copies ∠ABC onto a second panel ray XY forming ∠XYZ. (a) What criterion guarantees ∠XYZ = ∠ABC? (b) If he bisects ∠XYZ with ray YW, find ∠XYW.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) SSS criterion (by copying equal arc lengths and chord distances). (b) ∠XYW = 52° / 2 = 26°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Angle Derivations: 60°, 30°, 90°, 45°)

questions.question_text: Drawing an arc on a line and intersecting it with the same compass radius from the intersection point constructs an angle of:
How is a 45° angle systematically derived using constructions?
Explain why the first arc intersection step constructs an angle of exactly 60°.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Keeping the compass radius unchanged creates an equilateral triangle with 3 equal side lengths, and every interior angle of an equilateral triangle measures 60°.

questions.question_text: Outline the construction steps to obtain a 30° angle and a 15° angle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Construct a 60° angle using equilateral arc. 2) Bisect 60° angle to get 30°. 3) Bisect 30° angle to get 15°.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how to construct a 90° perpendicular angle at a given point P on line 'l' using compass and ruler.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) With center P, draw a semicircle intersecting line 'l' at A and B. 2) From A and B, draw arcs with radius > AP intersecting at C above P. 3) Draw line PC. Line PC is perpendicular to line 'l' at P (∠CPA = 90°).

questions.question_text: A solar panel installation requires mounting brackets at angles of 60°, 30°, and 45°. (a) Which basic angle is constructed first for 30°? (b) How is 45° obtained? (c) Find angle between 30° and 45° brackets.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 60° angle is constructed first. (b) 45° is obtained by constructing 90° and bisecting it. (c) Difference = 45° - 30° = 15°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Regular Hexagon & Architectural Patterns)

questions.question_text: How many equilateral triangles form a regular hexagon from its center point?
What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
Explain why stepping off the radius 6 times around a circle's circumference forms a regular hexagon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Stepping off radius 'r' creates 6 adjacent chord segments of length 'r'. Each central triangle has 3 sides equal to 'r' (equilateral), subtending 6 × 60° = 360° at center.

questions.question_text: What is a pointed arch in architecture and how is it constructed geometrically?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A pointed arch consists of two circular arcs meeting at a central point at the top, constructed from center points on the base support line.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how to construct a regular hexagon ABCDEF of side length 4 cm using ruler and compass.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Draw circle of radius r = 4 cm with center O. 2) Mark point A on circumference. 3) With compass set at 4 cm, draw arc from A to mark B on circle. 4) Move to B and mark C; continue stepping off points D, E, F. 5) Join AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA.

questions.question_text: An Islamic tile pattern uses a 6-pointed star rosette constructed inside a regular hexagon. (a) Find central angle of each of the 6 constituent equilateral triangles. (b) Find interior angle of hexagon. (c) Total sum of interior angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Central angle = 360° / 6 = 60°. (b) Interior angle = 2 × 60° = 120°. (c) Total sum = 6 × 120° = 720°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Tilings & Tangram Puzzles)

questions.question_text: What two strict requirements define a valid plane tiling (tessellation)?
options: A) Zero gaps and zero overlaps
questions.correct_answer: A) Zero gaps and zero overlaps

questions.question_text: How many total pieces comprise a traditional Chinese Tangram puzzle?
List the individual shapes and quantities of the 7 Tangram pieces.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 5 isosceles right triangles (2 large, 1 medium, 2 small), 1 square, and 1 parallelogram.

questions.question_text: Can regular pentagons tile a 2D plane completely without gaps? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Interior angle of regular pentagon is 108°. Since 360° is not divisible by 108° (3 × 108° = 324°), gaps remain at vertices.

questions.question_text: Explain which regular polygons can tile a plane by themselves (monohedral tessellation) and prove why using vertex angle sum.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Regular polygons tile if interior angle divides 360° completely: 1) Equilateral Triangle (60°): 6 × 60° = 360°. 2) Square (90°): 4 × 90° = 360°. 3) Regular Hexagon (120°): 3 × 120° = 360°. Only triangles, squares, and hexagons form monohedral regular tilings.

questions.question_text: A floor designer uses a square layout divided into a 7-piece Tangram set. (a) If area of square is 64 sq cm, find area of 7 pieces combined. (b) What fraction of area is formed by 2 large triangles? (c) Name all 4-sided shapes in Tangram.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total area = 64 sq cm (tessellation preserves total area). (b) Two large triangles form 1/2 of total area = 32 sq cm. (c) The square and the parallelogram (two 4-sided shapes).

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 7 Practice Paper (Weighing Scale & Mobile Models)

questions.question_text: In algebra, what does a letter symbol (variable) like 'x' or 'y' represent?
If a balanced weighing scale has (Sack + 2 kg) on LHS and 10 kg on RHS, what is the weight of the sack?
Explain the balance scale principle for maintaining equality in an equation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An equation represents a balanced scale. Performing the exact same operation (adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing equal amounts) on both sides maintains equality.

questions.question_text: A hanging mobile has total weight 16 kg. Left branch has 2 weights of 5 kg each. Right branch has 2 identical objects 'e'. Frame equation and solve for 'e'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Left weight = 10 kg. Right weight = 2e. Since mobile balances: 2e = 10 ⇒ e = 5 kg.

questions.question_text: Solve for x systematically and state balance operation at each step: 3x + 7 = 22.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) 3x + 7 = 22. 2) Subtract 7 from both sides (maintains balance): 3x = 22 - 7 ⇒ 3x = 15. 3) Divide both sides by 3 (maintains balance): x = 15 / 3 ⇒ x = 5. Check: 3(5) + 7 = 22 verified.

questions.question_text: A mobile puzzle has a top beam holding total weight 24 kg divided equally into 12 kg left and 12 kg right. Left side has 3 identical blocks 'b'. Right side has 2 blocks 'b' and a 4 kg weight. (a) Find 'b' from left side. (b) Verify right side balance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Left side: 3b = 12 ⇒ b = 4 kg. (b) Right side: 2b + 4 = 2(4) + 4 = 8 + 4 = 12 kg. Both sides balance at 12 kg.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 7 Practice Paper (Inverse Operations)

questions.question_text: What is the inverse operation of multiplication?
Solve: 5z + 2 = 17.
State the 4 inverse operation pairings used to isolate variables in linear equations.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Addition inverse is Subtraction (+a ↔ -a). 2) Subtraction inverse is Addition (-a ↔ +a). 3) Multiplication inverse is Division (×a ↔ ÷a). 4) Division inverse is Multiplication (÷a ↔ ×a).

questions.question_text: Given 4k + 1 = 13, find values of: (a) k, (b) 8k + 2, (c) 4k - 1.
Solve 5z + 2 = 3z - 4 systematically step-by-step with complete justification.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Subtract 3z from both sides: 5z - 3z + 2 = -4 ⇒ 2z + 2 = -4. 2) Subtract 2 from both sides: 2z = -6. 3) Divide both sides by 2: z = -3. Check: LHS = 5(-3)+2 = -13; RHS = 3(-3)-4 = -13. LHS = RHS verified.

questions.question_text: A taxi service charges fixed fee ₹800 plus ₹20 per km. Total bill is ₹2200. (a) Write cost equation for distance 'd'. (b) Solve for 'd'. (c) What is bill for 100 km?

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Chapter 7 Practice Paper (Function Machines)

questions.question_text: A function machine doubles an input 'x' and adds 5. What is the output expression?
If function machine output is 21 for 2x + 5, what was the input 'x'?
Explain how to run a function machine backward using inverse operations.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: To run backward, start with output value and apply the inverse of each operation in reverse order to determine the input.

questions.question_text: Function machine steps: Input x → Multiply by 3 → Subtract 4 → Output 11. Find input x.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Reverse steps: Output 11 → Add 4 (= 15) → Divide by 3 (= 5). Input x = 5.

questions.question_text: A complex function machine performs: Input x → Add 3 → Multiply result by 2 → Divide by 5 → Output 6. (a) Frame equation. (b) Solve for input x.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Equation: 2(x + 3) / 5 = 6. (b) Multiply by 5: 2(x + 3) = 30. Divide by 2: x + 3 = 15. Subtract 3: x = 12. Input x = 12.

questions.question_text: A temperature conversion machine converts Celsius (C) to Fahrenheit (F) via: F = (9/5)C + 32. (a) Find F when C = 25°C. (b) Run machine backward to find C when F = 95°F.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 7 Practice Paper (Algebraic Word Problems)

questions.question_text: One quarter of a number increased by 9 equals the number. What is the number?
The sum of three consecutive integers is 45. What is the middle integer?
Rohan's father is 4 years more than 3 times Rohan's age. If father is 40 years old, find Rohan's age.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Let Rohan's age be 'r'. Equation: 3r + 4 = 40 ⇒ 3r = 36 ⇒ r = 12 years.

questions.question_text: Perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 32 cm. Equal sides are 10 cm each. Find base length 'b'.
A rectangle has length (2x + 3) cm and width (x + 1) cm. Its perimeter is 38 cm. (a) Frame equation. (b) Find x. (c) Calculate length and width.

In a school library, total books = 450. Fiction books are twice non-fiction books, and reference books are 30 more than non-fiction. (a) Frame equation with x as non-fiction. (b) Find number of non-fiction, fiction, and reference books.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Non-fiction = x, Fiction = 2x, Reference = x + 30. Total = x + 2x + (x + 30) = 450 ⇒ 4x + 30 = 450. (b) 4x = 420 ⇒ x = 105 non-fiction. Fiction = 210, Reference = 135.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 7 Practice Paper (Error Analysis & Bījagaṇita History)

questions.question_text: What does the historical Indian term 'Bīja' mean in Bījagaṇita?
Which is the correct expansion of 3(x + 2)?
Identify and correct the mistake in: 4x + 6 = 10 ⇒ 4x = 10 + 6 = 16 ⇒ x = 4.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mistake: 6 was added instead of subtracted. Correct: 4x = 10 - 6 ⇒ 4x = 4 ⇒ x = 1.

questions.question_text: Explain the philosophical connection between a seed (bīja) and an unknown variable in Bījagaṇita.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Just as a complete tree is hidden inside a seed, the unknown answer is hidden inside an algebraic equation, awaiting systematic steps to grow and reveal itself.

questions.question_text: Correct three student errors: (i) 2(v - 4) = 6 ⇒ 2v - 4 = 6, (ii) 7 - 8z = 5 ⇒ 8z = 7 + 5, (iii) x/3 = 9 ⇒ x = 3.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (i) Correct expansion: 2v - 8 = 6 ⇒ 2v = 14 ⇒ v = 7. (ii) Correct transposition: 7 - 5 = 8z ⇒ 8z = 2 ⇒ z = 1/4. (iii) Multiply by 3: x = 9 × 3 = 27.

questions.question_text: A math student attempts to solve 4(x - 3) = 2x + 6. (a) Expand LHS correctly. (b) Transpose variable terms to LHS and constants to RHS. (c) Solve for x. (d) Verify solution.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) LHS = 4x - 12. (b) 4x - 2x = 6 + 12 ⇒ 2x = 18. (c) x = 9. (d) Verification: LHS = 4(9-3) = 4(6) = 24; RHS = 2(9)+6 = 18+6 = 24. LHS = RHS verified.
